oneLiner: Closed at 28,384.85 Friday, down 3.46% on the day and about 2.0% on the week, roughly 9.1% below the record close of about 31,224 set on October 6.
intro: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 28,384.85 on Friday, October 30, down 3.46% on the day and about 2.0% on the week, roughly 9.1% below its October 6 record close of about 31,224. This week's disappointing results from Alphabet, Amazon and Intel were blamed for reviving doubts about heavy AI spending and weighing on chip and mega-cap stocks. It was the index's third weekly loss in a row.

performance.heading: How the index has done
performance.body: The strip above tracks QQQ, the ETF that follows the Nasdaq-100, through the same week. The index rose 1.09% on Monday, but Friday's 3.46% drop left it down about 2.0% on the week. The longer-period cards show how this third weekly loss in a row sits against the longer trend.

chart.heading: The trend against its moving averages
chart.body: The daily chart above plots QQQ against its 50- and 200-day moving averages. After Friday's drop, the chart may show how close price sits to those lines and whether the slide from the October 6 record, now roughly 9% on the index, has paused or is still extending.

levels.heading: Where the nearby levels sit
levels.body: The October 6 record close of about 31,224 is the nearest marker above on the index, with Friday's close about 9.1% below it. Last week's close of 28,957.53 sits about 2.0% above Friday's. The Price zones and Key levels cards above show where the nearby levels sit on QQQ today.

signals.heading: Momentum in plain words
signals.body: Momentum may look strained after a third weekly loss in a row and Friday's 3.46% drop, which was led by chip and AI-linked stocks. Intel fell about 29% on the day, and Nvidia also fell. The panel above shows today's RSI and MACD readings on QQQ, which can differ from the index.

change.heading: The weekly and monthly pattern
change.body: Close to close, the index fell about 2.0% this week, after a loss of about 0.8% the week before and a 5.49% slide the week before that. It rose 1.09% on Monday and fell 3.46% on Friday. The tabs above show the daily, weekly and monthly changes on QQQ.

marketRead: The Nasdaq-100 ended the week at 28,384.85, down about 2.0% and roughly 9.1% below its October 6 record close of about 31,224. It was a week of big-company results. The index gained 1.09% on Monday, October 26, as Anthropic's public filing for a stock market listing gave AI shares a brief lift. Microsoft reported Azure cloud growth of about 48%, but Alphabet fell more than 12% on Thursday, October 29, after earnings missed estimates and free cash flow was negative again. On Friday, Amazon's earnings miss and heavy cash outflow, plus a weak outlook from Intel, which fell about 29%, were blamed for a wider rout in which Nvidia also fell.

Rates and inflation framed the backdrop. On Wednesday, October 28, the Federal Reserve held rates in a 10-2 vote, with two officials preferring a rise, and futures priced roughly an 85% chance of a hike at the December 9 meeting, as of that afternoon. September PCE inflation data, released Thursday, October 29, showed prices up 3.6% from a year earlier, with the core measure at 3.1%. The 10-year Treasury yield was about 4.9% on Friday, and oil stayed expensive, with U.S. crude above $100 a barrel.

We could not confirm a dated figure for the share of Nasdaq-100 members above their 200-day average, so none is shown. The optimistic case is that yields have eased to about 4.9%, Microsoft's cloud growth stayed strong at about 48%, and Friday's drop may already reflect much of the worry about AI cash burn. The cautious case is that three weekly losses in a row, a Fed that may raise rates in December and doubts over how AI spending will pay back could keep pressure on the mega-cap names that weigh heavily on the index.

The coming weeks may hinge on remaining big-company earnings, inflation data and the Fed's December 9 meeting, as well as on whether chip stocks steady after Friday's drop. Anthropic's planned stock market listing may also keep attention on AI spending.

points.label: Catalyst
points.text: Alphabet, Amazon and Intel results revived AI-spending worries; the index fell 3.46% on Friday.

points.label: Record
points.text: The index set a record close of about 31,224 on October 6; Friday's close sits about 9.1% below it.

points.label: Rates
points.text: The Fed held rates in a 10-2 vote on October 28; the 10-year yield was near 4.9% on Friday.

watchDown: Worries about AI cash burn spread from Alphabet, Amazon and Intel to other large technology names.
Rate-rise bets for the Fed's December 9 meeting build, pushing Treasury yields back toward 5%.
Oil prices climb further, keeping inflation worries alive and pressing on growth company valuations.
The index slips further below last week's close of 28,957.53.
watchUp: Chip stocks steady after Friday's sharp drop and Intel's plunge.
The 10-year yield stays below 5% and rate-rise bets for December cool.
Remaining big-company results ease the questions about AI spending returns.
The index recovers toward its October 6 record close of about 31,224.
